question: How do senescent cells contribute to the chronic inflammation seen in ageing?
answers: Through the factors they secrete, the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)
They release a mix of inflammatory secreted factors (SASP) such as cytokines and chemokines

receipt.quote: The SASP includes a variety of extracellular modulators, including cytokines, chemokines, proteases, pro‐fibrotic growth factors, lipids, and exosomes (EXOs), and it is one of the major contributors to the chronic inflammation that happens in aging (Basisty et al., 2020; Yin et al., 2021).
